Declare whether the business is part of a chain (formula retail) and provide the floor area in square feet. State that the restaurant will close by 2 AM and will not offer entertainment. Note that the project is in the NCT-24th-Mission district, the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District and the Calle 24 Special Use District, and that Planning confirmed (in step 1) compliance with the Calle 24 35% frontage rule. outcomes.original: Filing step: After CUA approval, file building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements and change of use, routing it to Planning, DPH and Fire. What to say: Submit the building permit application online via SF-DBI's permit portal with plans stamped by a licensed architect showing the kitchen layout, hood and fire suppression system, restrooms, ADA upgrades, finishes and equipment. State on the application that the use is a restaurant approved by Planning Commission under CUA case number [insert case number from step 4] and that the plans implement the conditions of approval in the Commission's motion. Ensure the application is routed to Planning (for zoning sign-off), DPH Environmental Health (for plan check) and Fire (for hood and place-of-assembly review if occupant load is 50 or more). The architect or expediter should coordinate plan check comments from all three departments and submit revised plans until approval.

What to say: Apply online through DPH's Environmental Health portal with two sets of scaled drawings, interior/exterior photos, and a menu describing preparation methods. State that the facility is a new restaurant with full cooking and request the new-restaurant plan check (8 hours, $2,207 flat fee as of FY 2026–27). ABC will mail a 30-day posting notice; post it at the premises in a front window visible from the street for 30 days and photograph it weekly. If the census tract is over its authorized number (which it is: 10 active on-sale licenses against 7 authorized), ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the city; start that process when ABC notifies you, working with Planning and the District Supervisor's office.…

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $6,700. Notes: Timeline is 120–300 days from CUA filing to approval for the conditional use authorization and health permit, the two approvals in the entitlement path given by the rules. Comparable restaurant CUAs with beer-and-wine service in this district took 28 days (a 2003 self-service restaurant across the street), 126 days (a 2011 full-service restaurant 51 m away), 133 days (a 2001 full-service restaurant next door at 43 m), and 408 days (a 2018 change from restaurant to restaurant with beer and wine at 57 m). The 408-day case is an outlier reflecting a more complex environmental review or continuances; typical timelines are 4–6 months when the application is complete and neighborhood outreach is documented. Cost is $3,100–$6,700 in government fees for the CUA (base fee approximately $3,100–$3,150 as of 2025, not in the catalog), health plan check ($2,207 for new restaurant, 8 hours) and health permit ($470). These figures are for the time and cost to obtain the two approvals when they are granted; they are not a time to a denial or a withdrawal. The building permit and ABC license are in insufficient-information status (the building permit because change of use and change of occupancy are not established, the ABC license because how the license will be obtained is not given), so their time and cost are not included here. If the Calle 24 SUD 35% frontage rule prohibits the project, there is no approval path and no timeline or cost applies.
